title: A rate limit whose slope exceeds its maxAmount is a burst control, and Grove uses that shape for execution venues rather than for held positions
content:
A.6.1.1.2.2.6.1.3.1.6.1.2.4.3 sets the Curve RLUSD/USDC swap limits at `maxAmount` 20 million, `slope` 100 million per day, `maxSlippage` 0.1%. Compare Aave: 50 million cap, 25 million per day.

The two ratios describe opposite risk postures. Aave's cap exceeds its daily slope, so the binding constraint is **time** — you can hold up to 50 million but rebuilding the budget takes two days. Curve's slope exceeds its cap fivefold, so the binding constraint is **size per burst** — no single swap may exceed 20 million, but the budget refills in roughly 4.8 hours, permitting several such swaps a day.

That is exactly the right shape for a venue used transiently. A swap does not accumulate exposure; it converts one asset into another and finishes. What must be bounded is the size of any one execution, because that is what determines price impact and how much a manipulated pool could extract. Total daily throughput is not the risk.

The accompanying `maxSlippage` of 0.1% is the third parameter completing the picture, and it connects to the code: `CurveLib` reverts with `max-slippage-not-set` if it is zero and uses it to derive the floor a relayer's `minAmountOut` must clear (A...2.1.2.8.1.2, A...2.1.2.8.1.4). A 20 million cap and a 0.1% tolerance are complementary — the cap keeps trades inside the range where 0.1% is achievable in this pool.

The generalisable reading: `maxAmount / slope` is the refill period, and whether it is long or short tells you whether governance is limiting accumulation or limiting single-shot impact.
description: The Curve RLUSD/USDC swap limit is 20 million with a 100 million per day slope — refilling in under five hours — the inverse of the Aave shape where the cap exceeds the daily slope.
